questions.question: 1. What happens when running.size >= maxConcurrency inside processQueue()?
options: AThe oldest running task is preempted to make room.
BprocessQueue() returns early; queued tasks stay in the queue.
CThe queue is sorted again and the highest-priority task is forced to run.
DAn error is thrown telling the caller to wait.
questions.explanation: Correct! The scheduler uses early return as a backpressure gate. Tasks remain in the queue until a running task finishes and frees a concurrency slot.

questions.question: 2. How does task cancellation differ for a queued task vs a running task?
options: ABoth are aborted via AbortController; only the timing differs.
BQueued tasks are paused; running tasks are removed from the Map.
CRunning tasks call controller.abort(); queued tasks are spliced out of the array.
DThere is no difference; cancel() behaves identically in both cases.
questions.explanation: Correct! Running tasks need cooperative cancellation via AbortController. Queued tasks have not started, so removing them from the queue is sufficient.

questions.question: 3. In the engine's executeNode(), when are outgoing connections traversed?
options: AImmediately before the node executor runs, to pre-fetch downstream nodes.
BOnly if the node has no incoming connections, as a starting-node optimization.
CAfter the node executor succeeds and its result is stored in nodeResults.
DIn the finally block so they run even when the node fails.
questions.explanation: Correct! Outgoing connections are traversed inside the try block, after the result is stored. If the node fails, the catch throws before downstream nodes are reached.
